morph: a jack-in-the-box pops a glowing lamp, the fire crew double-takes, and the glowing strokes arrange into 燈

promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 燈 (lamp), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a chunky toy fire engine and its crew with a mind-of-its-own hose, and a desk lamp in a jack-in-the-box. Soft dusk-lilac backdrop (still bright); the glyph is warm glowing amber-yellow. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a stubby red toy fire engine rolls in, its blue siren lamp spinning; the voice says the first 燈 as a gift box in front of it rattles. 1.5-3.0s: the lid bursts open and a springy toy desk lamp boings out with a bulb head; the engine reverses with a startled squeak and the little crew figures tumble over. The voice says the second 燈 as the lamp's glow spills into the left fire radical. 3.0-4.5s: the engine's hose wriggles, accidentally bends the lamp's neck, and the light drops down into the right strokes, completing 燈. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 電燈 (ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄉㄥ) as the lamp's bulb flicks on with a bright warm glow and little sparkles around it, no strobing. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is still; the lamp bows gently and the engine lights its siren in a slow friendly blink. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 燈、燈、電燈 (ㄉㄥ、ㄉㄥ、ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄉㄥ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, and stop; no other speech, subtitles or loud music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 燈 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 小外星人開著飛碟想用牽引光束搶走一盞巨大的玩具立燈，結果先把自己吸得翻過來，氣得後仰衝刺一頭撞上燈柱，撞落的火花疊成左邊的火、燈架零件掉成右邊的登，壓扁的飛碟搖搖晃晃拉一下拉繩，整個「燈」字就亮了起來。
object: a giant unlit toy floor lamp with a round bulb head, two bent arms and a tall post on a round base, standing at the far right of the frame
morph: the saucer's crash shakes the lamp loose: four glowing sparks tumble left and stack into the 火 radical, while the lamp's two bent arms, post and round base drop straight down on the right and settle into 登, completing 燈; a dangling pull-cord then switches the whole glyph on in warm amber light
creativeAngle: 改走「衝刺撞擊」的實體笑料：先讓外星人的牽引光束吸錯對象（吸到自己）作為失敗鋪陳，再以後仰助跑、全速撞燈柱的大 BONK 把燈的零件震落成字，撞落的火花對應火部、燈架對應登部，一目了然。最後用拉繩「喀」一聲讓整個字像電燈一樣亮起，正好配合口白「電燈」，聲音與畫面同一個故事；與前一版靜態發光的檯燈、消防車開箱完全不同。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip teaching the single Traditional Chinese glyph 燈 (lamp). Pale cream-sky background, nothing busy behind. Cast: a small green cartoon alien with big round eyes piloting a chunky toy flying saucer with a wobbly tractor-beam nozzle underneath, and one giant unlit toy floor lamp (round gray bulb head, two bent arms, tall post, round base) standing at the far right.

0.0–1.3s: The saucer hovers at the far left. The alien spots the giant lamp, eyes go huge, it points eagerly with both hands and rubs them together. The off-screen voice says the first 燈 as the saucer rattles with excitement and the lamp's bulb gives a small dull glint.

1.3–2.6s: The alien slams a big red button. A green tractor beam shoots out, but curls straight back up and grabs the saucer itself, flipping it upside down with the alien dangling by its boots, arms flailing. The beam sputters off and the saucer plops back down with a squeak. The alien frowns, rolls up its sleeves.

2.6–3.6s: Wind-up: the saucer tilts way back, its little landing feet dig in with a scrape, a frozen beat of anticipation, then it rockets across the whole frame left to right and slams into the lamp post. Big squashy cartoon BONK: the saucer squashes flat, the lamp wobbles like a bell.

3.6–4.8s: The crash shakes the lamp apart in clean pieces. Four glowing sparks tumble down on the left and stack into the 火 radical. On the right the two bent arms drop first into the top of 登, then the tall post and round base settle beneath them as 豆. The voice says the second 燈 exactly as the last stroke snaps into place, forming one correctly written 燈 in saturated amber-orange strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with margins.

4.8–5.5s: The flattened saucer wobbles out from behind the glyph like a pancake and pops back round. The alien staggers out dizzy with a huge grin, little stars circling its head.

5.5–8.0s: Final hold, glyph perfectly still. A single lamp pull-cord dangles beside the glyph. The alien reaches up and tugs it: click. The voice says 電燈 exactly as the entire glyph 燈 flicks on with a warm golden glow and a soft halo, steady, no strobing. The alien does a tiny victory wiggle in the saucer away from the strokes, never covering them.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 燈、燈、電燈 (ㄉㄥ、ㄉㄥ、ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄉㄥ). Character, short pause, character, then the word once, then stop. No other speech, no subtitles, no loud music; soft cartoon squeak and bonk sounds only. The glyph 燈 is the only text on screen: no captions, labels, watermark, logos or flashing effects. No real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon creatures.
